text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The High Representative to Bosnia, Carl Bildt, plans to request that the international commununity refuse to recognise any Bosnian ambassador who is not appointed by the collective presidency by July 1, diplomatic sources say.
- Dividing the assets of former Yugoslavia is a complex issue but should be resolved soon, says Sir Arthur Watts, special negotiator for succession.

- The ombudsmen for the Moslem-Croat federation published a report on human rights violations saying the majority of abuses were committed by government authorities over tenancy rights to state-owned property.
- The crime rate in the Moslem-Croat federation decreased in April while suicides and car accidents increased, federation interior ministry says.
- A mass grave containing the bodies of 171 Moslem and Croats killed in 1992 has been discovered in the village of Hrgar in the Bihac region, interior ministry says.
- The Nato-led Stabilisation Force (SFOR) was ready to arrest indicted war criminal Radovan Karadzic last week but he did not dare leave his home, anonymous sources tell newspaper.

- The U.S. Agency for International Development has granted 200 million dollars to assist Bosnian companies. The funds will be allocated after Washington reviews how Bosnian factions are complying with the Dayton peace treaty, says U.S. official. -- Sarajevo newsroom +387 81 663
